recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If FHIRPath or validator tooling later gains sequence-aware grouping support, the second rule can be reconsidered as a new tooling/spec enhancement; no current FHIR-core source correction is needed for FHIR-13400.
issue_request: FHIR-13400 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core StructureDefinition change request asking for constraints that prohibit sliceName on a true snapshot or differential root element and prohibit snapshot sliceName values unless a preceding element in the same path hierarchy declares slicing.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 5dfb9237e7c6c0550099bc8feedb68b7a8c85eaf, matching svn revision 14484 cited in Jira, added invariant 23 to the StructureDefinition spreadsheet: no sliceName on root. The current generated StructureDefinition source preserves this as error-level invariant sdf-23 and applies it to both snapshot.element and differential.element.
additional_context: The Jira resolution explicitly recognized that a differential may begin at a non-root subnode, so the invariant must test for an actual root path rather than the first element in the list. It also accepted the same-path predecessor rule but stated that it could not be expressed in FHIRPath without grouping or a previous-node axis. Current ElementDefinition slicing prose still defines a slice set as following elements with the same path after a slicing entry.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source already implements the enforceable path-based root sliceName rule, and adding an approximate duplicate invariant for the sequence-aware rule would go beyond the applied resolution and could create false validation failures.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue about root sliceName values in generated profiles; it reinforces that root sliceNames are invalid but was a separate spreadsheet/tooling issue and was not decided here.
